name: Margaret Esherick House
features: Deep recessed window walls in a plain stucco box; wooden shutters control light and view separately.

extras.file: File:Elevations - Margaret Esherick House, 204 Sunrise Lane, Philadelphia, Philadelphia County, PA HABS PA-6775 (sheet 2 of 4).tif
File:Details - Margaret Esherick House, 204 Sunrise Lane, Philadelphia, Philadelphia County, PA HABS PA-6775 (sheet 4 of 4).tif

note: Several free exterior photos (public domain) plus HABS measured drawings.

name: Frey House II
features: Small glass and steel box built around a boulder on the mountainside, under a sloping corrugated metal roof.
note: Only one free photo (4123x2748), seen from the Museum Trail; check it reads well as a tile.

name: Stahl House (Case Study House #22)
features: L-shaped steel and glass pavilion cantilevered over the Hollywood Hills, with deep flat roof overhangs.

photos.file: File:Julius Shulman - Case Study House 22, Arts & Architecture, June 1960 (page 15 crop 3).jpg

note: Many free photos, including public-domain Julius Shulman photos from Arts & Architecture (1960).

name: Hooper House II
features: Long fieldstone wall with an opening through its middle into a courtyard; glass faces the landscape behind.
note: Only one free photo (2592x1944), of the rear facade by the living room; filed under Category:Buildings by Marcel Breuer, no own category. Year 1959 from Breuer catalogues; Commons files it under 'Houses built in Maryland in 1960'.

name: Douglas House
features: White house on a steep slope to Lake Michigan, entered by a bridge at roof level; glass faces the lake.
note: One free photo (1719x2183, portrait) plus a section drawing.

name: Chemosphere (Malin Residence)
features: Octagonal house balanced on a single concrete column on a steep hillside, reached by a funicular.
note: Several free exterior photos.

name: Elrod House
features: Circular living room under a concrete roof of radiating wedges with glass between them, built into desert boulders.

photos.file: File:ELROD HOUSE, PALM SPRINGS, RIVERSIDE COUNTY, CA.jpg

note: One free photo (2784x1848); private house, check it shows the building clearly rather than just the gate.

name: Upper Lawn Pavilion
features: Weekend house: a timber and glass box set on and inside the old stone walls of a farm cottage.

photos.file: File:Tisbury, Font Hill Estate, Upper Lawn Pavilion (Solar Pavilion), 2010.jpg
File:The smithsons, alison and peter smithson, upper lawn pavilion, 1959-1962 (5387352719).jpg
File:The smithsons, alison and peter smithson, upper lawn pavilion, 1959-1962 (5395119654).jpg

note: Free square photos (CC BY 2.0), from Flickr. Also known as the Solar Pavilion. Movement 'Brutalism' in the sense of the Smithsons' New Brutalism.

name: Bavinger House
features: Rough stone wall spiralling up around a central mast that hangs the roof by cables; demolished 2016.
note: One public-domain exterior photo (3072x2304). The house was demolished in 2016. Goff's organic architecture has no exact match in the movement list; 'Expressionism' is the nearest.

name: Hopkins House
features: Two-storey steel-frame and glass box, entered by a bridge from the street at upper level; open plan inside.
note: 49a Downshire Hill, Hampstead. Several free photos.

name: Dirty House
features: Former warehouse painted dark with flush mirrored windows; a thin roof seems to float over a glazed top floor.
note: House and studio for artists Tim Noble and Sue Webster, Chance Street. The 'reflection' file is a close-up of a window.

name: Casa Ugalde
features: White walls fanned out across a hillside toward the sea, shaped around the views and existing trees.

photos.file: File:194 Casa Ugalde, c. Torrenova (Caldes d'Estrac).JPG

note: One free photo (1600x1200); private house, check how much of the building it shows.

name: Casa Gaspar
features: White walled square closed to the outside; a higher central band opens to two courtyards with a pool.
note: One free exterior photo (1600x1067), plus a patio photo (File:Casa gaspar patio.jpg, 697x1600, CC BY 2.0). In Zahora, municipality of Vejer de la Frontera.

name: Casa De Blas
features: A light white steel table with a glass box beneath, set on a heavy concrete podium on a hilltop.

photos.file: File:Casa De Blas Fotógrafo- Hisao Suzuki.jpg

note: One photo (2730x2176) credited to photographer Hisao Suzuki and marked CC BY-SA 3.0; worth checking the licence was granted by the photographer before using.

name: Das Gelbe Haus
features: Old village house stripped to its stone walls, painted white, with a new roof and one central timber column inside.
note: Not a house but a small exhibition building in a converted village house; included as a small building. One free photo (2740x3653).

name: Villa Schreiner
features: Low timber house on a modular grid, with Japanese-influenced post-and-beam structure and sliding walls.
note: One free photo (3264x2448).

name: Haus Gugalun
features: Old log farmhouse extended into the slope with new timber rooms under one continuous gable roof.
note: Ten free photos of all sides.

name: Walsh Street House (Boyd House II)
features: Two wings across a central courtyard under one roof hung on steel cables; mostly closed to the street.
note: Only one exterior photo (3508x2081), described as 'Front gate at street level'; check it shows enough of the street front. If not, this is a drawing candidate. Good free plan, section and 3D drawings exist.

name: Sea Ranch Condominium One
features: Ten timber-clad units clustered under steep single-pitch roofs that follow the wind-swept coastal meadow.

photos.file: File:Sea Ranch. Veduta del Condominium 1 verso l'oceano Pacifico.jpg
File:Sea Ranch. Veduta con il Condominium 1.jpg
File:Condominium One, Sea Ranch Condominiums, Sea Ranch, CA.JPG
File:Condominium 1, 110-128 Sea Walk Dr., Sea Ranch, CA 7-5-2010 7-07-18 PM.JPG

note: Several free photos.

name: House VI (Frank Residence)
features: House generated by a grid of planes and columns; an upside-down staircase and slots cut through floors and walls.

photos.file: File:House VI in Cornwall, Connecticut. Architect Peter Eisenman.tif

note: One photo taken in 1977 (1627x1055, TIFF), CC BY-SA 4.0. There is also File:Peter Eisenman House VI.png (1200x900, CC BY-SA 4.0) of uncertain content. Eisenman's houses are usually called post-structuralist or proto-deconstructivist; 'Deconstructivism' is the nearest in the list.

name: Healy Guest House (Cocoon House)
features: Small guest house on the bayou with a sagging roof hung like a cocoon between steel straps; louvred walls.

photos.file: File:Cocoon House (Paul Rudolph and Ralph Twitchell, Architects).jpg
File:Cocoon House 2 (Paul Rudolph and Ralph Twitchell, Architects).jpg
File:Cocoon House 3 (Paul Rudolph and Ralph Twitchell, Architects).jpg

extras.file: File:Healy Guest House (Cocoon House) - Conceptual Drawing - Paul Rudolph 1949.jpg
File:Healy Guest House (Cocoon House) - Floor Plan - Paul Rudolph, Architect.jpg
File:Cocoon House - Site Plan (Paul Rudolph, Architect, FAIA).jpg

note: Three free photos plus public-domain plans and a concept sketch. Siesta Key, Sarasota.

name: Gwathmey Residence and Studio
features: Two cedar-clad volumes cut from cubes and cylinders, with sharply sloped roofs and a curved stair.
note: No free photo on Commons. Sources describe cubes, cylinders and slanted roofs in vertical cedar, but I could not establish the exact arrangement of the cuts, curved stair and windows on each face well enough to draw it. Design 1965, completed 1966–67.

name: Can Feliz
features: Utzon's second Mallorca house: local sandstone blocks under one tiled roof, with three tall bay windows to the sea.
note: No free photo on Commons. Wikipedia describes three blocks under one tiled roof around a terrace, three lofty bay windows and a covered south terrace, but not enough to draw the elevation accurately. Near Portopetro / S'Horta (municipality of Santanyí; check).

name: Creek Vean
by: Team 4 (Norman Foster, Wendy Cheesman, Richard Rogers, Su Brumwell)
features: Two wings stepped down a creek-side slope either side of a public stair; planted roofs let it sink into the hill.
note: Only free photo is File:Creek Vean House Pill Creek.jpg (531x600, CC BY-SA 2.0), below the 800px minimum. The stepped section and roof gardens are documented, but I could not pin down the creek elevation well enough to draw it. Team 4's first building.

name: Hanselmann House
features: Deconstructed white cube reached by an elevated walkway through a layered front; Graves's first commission.
note: No free photo found on Commons. Sources describe a deconstructed white cube, a bridge-like elevated walkway to the entrance and layered exterior spaces (double square in plan, double cube in volume), but not enough to draw each face accurately. Built 1967–71; year given as design year 1967.

name: Walker Guest House
features: 24-foot-square pavilion on an 8-foot grid; wooden wall panels swing up as awnings, balanced by cannonball weights.

extras.file: File:Paul Rudolph - Walker Guest House Floorplan.jpg

view: Elevation of one side: three 8-foot bays in the light frame, the left panel raised as an awning and the other two closed; the side panels propped out flat at roof level; the cannonball counterweights hanging at the corners.
note: No free photo on Commons (only the floor plan, 919x751). Built 1952–53 on Sanibel Island; sold in 2019, dismantled and moved to California. A full-size replica was built in 2015 by the Sarasota Architectural Foundation. Cannonball weights shown schematically at the corners.

name: Marie Short House
features: Two near-identical timber pavilions on stilts under curved corrugated metal roofs; louvres adjust air and light.
view: End elevation of the two parallel pavilions side by side: shallow roofs with rounded ridges, louvred end walls, floors raised about a metre on stumps.
note: No free photo on Commons. Sources give 1974 or 1975; Murcutt bought and extended it in 1980. Near Kempsey (Crescent Head), NSW; on the State Heritage Register. The pavilions are offset ('slipped') in plan, which an end elevation does not show; the louvre bands are schematic.

name: Delta Shelter
features: Steel-clad cabin on four steel columns above a flood plain; four 10 by 18 ft steel shutters roll across to close it up.
view: Front elevation: the two-storey steel box raised on four columns over a small ground-floor base, one shutter rolled aside along its rails to show the glazing, the other closed.
note: No free photo on Commons. About 200 sq ft footprint and about 1,000 sq ft over three levels, on a 100-year flood plain by the Methow River; shutters are human-powered. Window pattern behind the shutter is schematic.

name: Smith House
features: White house closed to the road, open to the water through three storeys of glass; the fireplace pushes through.
note: No free photo on Commons. Sources confirm a ramp to the entrance on the closed land side, a three-level glass enclosure on the water side and a painted brick fireplace pushing out through the mullions, but I could not confirm how the floor slabs, double-height living room and chimney sit in the water elevation, so I did not draw it (a generic glass box with a chimney would mislead).

name: Casa Rotonda
features: Three-level cylindrical house split north–south by a cut that brings daylight down from the roof.

photos.file: File:Stabio, Casa Medici (arch. Mario Botta 1980-82) - panoramio.jpg

note: On Commons the photos are titled 'Casa Medici' (the clients were Liliana and Ovidio Medici); same building, 1980–82. Don't confuse with Commons files 'Casa Rotonda 1/2.jpg', which show a different building in Corzoneso.

name: 22 Parkside (Rogers House)
features: Steel portal frames closed by glass ends: a house and a studio either side of a garden court.
note: Built for Rogers's parents in Wimbledon, 1968–69. One free photo at 3500x2417; two more at 640px are too small. Don't confuse with 'File:22 Parkside, Cambridge.jpg', a different building. Facts from general knowledge of the house; check before use.

name: Casa Kalmann
features: Concrete house set into a steep slope above Lake Maggiore, with a pavilion looking out over the lake.
note: Several free photos (1974–76, per the Commons descriptions). Spelled Kalman or Kalmann. Facts from Commons descriptions and general knowledge; check before use.

name: Villa Busk
features: A 40 m concrete and timber wing on bedrock, linked by a glazed bridge to a four-storey tower with a pyramid roof.
view: Side elevation across the slope: the four-storey tower with its pyramid roof on the lower ground, the glazed diagonal-braced bridge, and the long low main wing on the rock.
note: No free photo on Commons. On Kjønnøya, Bamble; built 1987–90; listed by Riksantikvaren in 1993. Massing follows the written description (40 m wing, four-storey tower, freestanding glazed bridge with diagonal timber structure); window patterns and the wing's roof line are left plain because no source gives them. Original drawings are in the Nasjonalmuseet collection (not free).

name: Breuer House II
features: Breuer's own timber house, cantilevered out from a smaller base, with a deck hung on steel cables.
note: One free photo at 1024x680 (counts under the 800px rule). Built 1947–48. Facts from general knowledge of the house; the cantilever and cable-hung deck are well published but check before use.

name: Noyes House
features: Two long fieldstone walls with glass pavilions between them, wrapped around an open central courtyard.
note: One free photo at 1024x680 (counts under the 800px rule). Eliot Noyes's own house (Noyes House II). Facts from general knowledge; check before use.

name: Stretto House
features: Four concrete-block 'spatial dams' with light curved metal roofs flowing between them, beside three ponds.
note: No free photo on Commons. Sources confirm four sections, concrete-block dams and curved lead-coated copper roofs by three ponds, but not the profile and stepping of the roofs in elevation, so I did not draw it. Dates given as 1989–91 (Holl) or 1992 (monograph); inspired by Bartók's Music for Strings, Percussion and Celesta.

name: Simpson-Lee House
features: Single-storey steel and glass pavilions on a bush track; angled roofs collect rainwater; pool to the north.
note: No free photo of this house on Commons. Careful: 'Simpson-Lee House I' on Commons (File:Simpson Lee House.jpg and the NSW heritage photos) is a different house for the same clients, by Arthur Baldwinson (1958–62). The roof angle, pavilion sizes and bridge position aren't described closely enough to draw. On the NSW State Heritage Register.

name: Ball-Eastaway House
features: Corrugated-iron pavilion with a gently curved roof, on slender steel columns set into a sandstone ledge.
note: No free photo on Commons. Sources confirm the raised pavilion on steel columns over sandstone and a gently curved roof, but not which way the roof curves or how the end walls and decks look, so I did not draw it. Wilkinson Award 1984; on the NSW State Heritage Register.

name: Casa Beires
features: Nicknamed the 'bomb house': a white box broken open by folded glass walls around a small courtyard.
note: No free photo on Commons. Sources describe a prism broken by glassy folds around a courtyard, but not the geometry of the folds closely enough to draw. Built 1973–76 (Wikipedia's list gives 1964, probably the commission).

name: House with One Wall
features: Two homes split by one folded concrete wall that carries all the floors; every other wall is glass.
note: No free photo on Commons. Elongated hexagonal plan, fully glazed on all six sides, in Witikon; the wall's course changes on every floor, which I could not establish well enough to draw.

name: Möbius House
features: Low, elongated house whose rooms follow a Möbius loop in plan and section; concrete and glass swap roles along it.
note: No free photo on Commons. The interlocking loop of folded concrete and glass is hard to show in one elevation and sources don't give the faces in detail; not drawn.

name: Number 11 (Bawa's house)
features: Four small bungalows on 33rd Lane joined over 40 years into one house of courtyards, with a tower of roof terraces.
note: Inward-looking house with almost no street face. Commons has File:Eingangsbereich-Wohnhaus Geoffrey Bawa-Colombo.jpg (2000x2667, CC BY-SA 4.0, 'Entrance area at the Geoffrey Bawa Trust'); it may show the entrance rather than the outside, so check it. Year is approximate: Bawa converted it from 1958 until the late 1990s; please confirm before use.

name: Ena de Silva House
features: Rooms round an inward-looking courtyard under red tile roofs on satinwood columns; Sinhalese house meets modern plan.
note: No free photo found. Built 1960–62 in Colombo; dismantled and rebuilt at Lunuganga, completed in 2016 (photos of the rebuilt house may appear under Category:Lunuganga Estate; I didn't find one named for it). Courtyard plan is hard to show in one elevation; not drawn.

name: Carter/Tucker House
features: Three-level box set into a sand dune, screened in horizontal cedar battens that open as flaps on gas struts.
view: Long elevation: the rectangular batten-clad box set into the side of the dune, with two batten flaps raised on the living level to show the glazing behind.
note: No free photo on Commons. Weekend house and studio for a photographer: bedroom level, living level and roof deck inside braced steel portal frames with glazed walls. Overall proportions and flap positions are schematic; the batten skin and dune setting are from the sources.
